title: Arrival: the airport & your residence card
intro:
If you enter Japan to live there for the mid to long term (for work, study, as a spouse and so on), immigration will check your passport and your visa or Certificate of Eligibility. At the major international airports, such as Narita, Haneda, Kansai and Chubu, you are usually handed your residence card ({在留[ざいりゅう]カード}) on the spot. If you arrive elsewhere, your passport is stamped and the card is sent to you after you register your address.

The residence card is your main ID in Japan. Adults are required to carry it at all times, and you will need it for almost every procedure: the ward office, bank, phone, apartment and job. Check it carefully as soon as you receive it. It shows your status of residence ({在留[ざいりゅう]資格[しかく]}), your period of stay ({在留[ざいりゅう]期間[きかん]}), and whether you are allowed to work.

After you find a place to live, you must register your address at the municipal office within 14 days (see the next unit).

To extend your stay, you apply to a regional immigration office before your period of stay ends; applications can generally be made from a few months before expiry. Requirements change, so always confirm the current rules with the Immigration Services Agency ({出入国[しゅつにゅうこく]在留[ざいりゅう]管理庁[かんりちょう]}). If you plan to leave Japan temporarily and come back, check the re-entry rules before you travel.

Practical tip: airports have counters where you can send heavy luggage to your new address by courier, so you can travel into the city light.

tips: Put your residence card expiry date in your calendar with a reminder several months ahead. Overstaying, even by accident, is a serious problem.
Check the work permission line on the card. If it is restricted, do not take on work outside what your status allows.
Keep digital copies of your passport, residence card and visa documents somewhere safe.
Immigration offices can be crowded. Many procedures can now be started online; check the Immigration Services Agency website first.
When you report a change, such as a new employer or a lost card, there are usually strict deadlines. Look them up the moment something changes.
